title: Client Onboarding Software: Top Tools for 2026 (and Where AI Video Fits)
summary: Compare top client onboarding software for 2026. See how AI humans handle kickoffs and walkthroughs portals were never designed for.
body_text: Client onboarding software: tools for 2026 (and where AI video fits) In SaaS, two nearly identical deals can age very differently. Two companies close with similar customers on the same day. Both have capable products, fair pricing, and a customer success team eager to help. Six months later, one company is renewing and expanding; the other is fielding a cancellation request. The deals were nearly identical, so the difference traces back to what happened in the first ninety days after signing. The first ninety days are when renewals are often decided. In Forrester's onboarding analysis , Principal Analyst Shari Srebnick puts it plainly, "The decision to renew is made in the first 90 days of the post-sale journey, making onboarding success a leading indicator of the future health of that customer relationship." A strong first ninety days builds the renewal foundation. Client onboarding software provides the first 90 days with a repeatable operating model. The category covers task coordination, shared customer workspaces, implementation governance, and time-to-value tracking. But portals and task trackers were never designed for the human-facing moments around the workflow, including kickoff calls and setup walkthroughs. Tavus, the human computing company behind Tavus PALs , builds full-stack PALs that see, hear, understand, and respond in real-time conversations. In onboarding, real-time conversational video is the delivery surface for those moments. Client onboarding software, defined Client onboarding software, as used in this guide, is a platform for managing the structured process of moving a new customer from contract signing to full live status. That includes project planning, task coordination, customer communication, milestone tracking, and time-to-value measurement. A customer onboarding portal can sit at the center of that process. It functions as a shared, branded workspace where SaaS companies guide new customers through their first 30-90 days, centralizing milestones, training resources, and progress tracking into a single source of truth for both the customer success manager (CSM) and the customer. The shared account-level workspace is especially important in B2B motions. In many B2B rollouts, onboarding involves multiple stakeholders and a higher expectation that the customer will see measurable value. A self-guided consumer signup differs sharply from rolling out a platform across a buyer's organization, where procurement, IT, and end users all need different things at different times. The B2B case for client onboarding software Time-to-value can shape retention risk. When customers reach a real value milestone early, they often have a clearer reason to keep investing attention, budget, and internal political capital. When they do not, risk can rise quickly. The onboarding period is when your product has to move from purchased promise to operational habit. Onboarding is also the front door to your largest revenue source. Forrester's B2B service research reports that 73% of B2B revenue originates from current customers, which puts the post-sale motion directly inside the revenue engine. Consistency is another reason teams invest in structured onboarding: when every account follows a tested sequence, quality can depend less on which CSM picked it up. Core features to look for in client onboarding software A handful of capabilities show up consistently in client onboarding guides , especially when teams are comparing purpose-built onboarding platforms with general project tools pressed into service. Client portals and shared workspaces: Branded workspaces where clients check progress, complete tasks, and upload files. Task and milestone tracking: Assignable tasks with dependencies and due dates spanning internal team members and client stakeholders, often structured as Mutual Action Plans. Automated workflows and reminders: Rules-based triggers that advance customers through onboarding stages, plus conditional logic, customer relationship management (CRM)-triggered project creation on deal close, and follow-ups when tasks stall. Reporting and health dashboards: Real-time metrics for leadership, with time-to-value, activation rates, drop-offs, and engagement trends feeding into customer health scoring. CRM and project tool integrations: Connectors to tools such as Salesforce, HubSpot, and Pipedrive that prefill forms, launch projects on deal close, and write milestones back to the customer record. Portals, milestone tracking, workflow automation, dashboards, and CRM integrations can give customer launch work a more repeatable operating model. Client onboarding software examples for 2026 The tools below are examples from the client onboarding category and adjacent customer success suites. They illustrate the tradeoffs B2B teams may compare heading into 2026. Implementation-oriented teams often compare GUIDEcx, Rocketlane, and OnRamp first. GUIDEcx fits sales-to-implementation handoffs and complex, multi-stakeholder implementations where customer collaboration, project visibility, and implementation governance matter. Rocketlane sits at the overlap between onboarding and professional services delivery, where teams need onboarding workflows alongside broader delivery controls. OnRamp is a more natural fit when a team wants centralized onboarding workflows and a consistent process at scale without building a full professional services automation (PSA) layer. Dock serves customer success teams that want reusable templates and visibility into stakeholder engagement through a lightweight portal experience. For companies buying a broader customer success suite, Planhat and Gainsight place onboarding inside a wider customer success motion. Across GUIDEcx, Rocketlane, OnRamp, Dock, Planhat, and Gainsight, the core value is workflow coordination. The human-facing conversations that surround the workflow still fall to a person. Client onboarding software vs. user onboarding software A common buyer mistake is treating onboarding as one category and picking the wrong type of tool for the motion. User onboarding software focuses on the in-product journey, guiding individual users from signup to first success through in-app tooltips, product tours, and checklists. Client onboarding software handles contract-to-kickoff workflows and implementation at the account level. Use case decides the category. Digital adoption platforms serve product-led growth: low-cost subscription products where users orient themselves with tooltips. Client onboarding platforms serve implementations that need collaboration and accountability from internal and external stakeholders, where the process takes weeks or months. The difference between account-level onboarding and user-level onboarding has teeth. Client onboarding addresses the buyer level, persuading the customer that their purchase was a sound business decision, while user onboarding addresses the practitioner level. When the buyer stays emotionally invested, the account can survive slower practitioner adoption. Choosing the right client onboarding software for your team Matching the tool to your delivery model is the first and most consequential decision. High-touch B2B motions often call for client portals and project plans: GUIDEcx, Rocketlane, OnRamp, Dock. Self-serve and product-led growth (PLG) motions typically lean toward in-app guidance tools because the economics and customer expectations differ. Team size and volume constrain what's feasible. A small team with a few complex enterprise launches may need deep project governance more than broad automation. A high-volume SaaS team may need templated portals, automated reminders, and clear escalation rules. A professional services organization may need PSA depth, while a customer success-led team may value customer health signals and stakeholder engagement tracking. Evaluate pricing against delivery complexity, implementation volume, and the amount of manual coordination the platform removes. Some tools use published tiers, others use custom contracts, and AI features may be packaged separately from the base onboarding workflow. The right question is whether the platform removes enough manual coordination to fit your goals for time-to-value, consistency, and account coverage. AI video's role in client onboarding software Most onboarding stacks share a blind spot. The portal coordinates tasks, the dashboard tracks health, the workflow fires reminders, and a human still has to run the kickoff call, the training session, and every "let me walk you through this" moment. Kickoff calls, training sessions, and guided setup conversations are where customers feel understood or feel processed, and they've always required a person on the other end. Real-time PAL guidance adds a conversational layer to the onboarding stack. Tavus builds full-stack PALs that see, hear, understand, and respond in real-time conversations. It explicitly lists "guided onboarding and support portals that walk users through setup, troubleshooting, or account verification with empathetic, adaptive guidance" as a core use case for its Conversational Video Interface (CVI) . In practice, PAL guidance appears at the moments CSMs repeat most often: kickoff, setup, and walkthroughs. A new account can get a face-to-face kickoff conversation that walks through goals, timelines, and first steps. A stakeholder logging in outside the next scheduled CSM session can get guided onboarding support instead of waiting for the next calendar opening. The repetitive setup explanations and configuration walkthroughs are candidates for PAL support. The CSM still owns the high-judgment relationship work, while a PAL for onboarding can cover routine guided-onboarding moments around setup and troubleshooting. A closed-loop behavioral stack runs underneath each conversation. Sparrow-1 governs conversational flow, Raven-1 perceives and fuses the other person's emotional and attentional signals, the large language model (LLM) layer reasons about what to say and do next, and Phoenix-4 renders responsive facial behavior. Sparrow-1 achieves 55ms median floor-prediction latency with 100% precision and zero interruptions across 28 challenging real-world conversational samples. Picture a new admin who trails off mid-sentence, trying to find a setting. Sparrow-1, the conversational flow model, holds the floor open without cutting in. As the admin works through a confusing step, Raven-1, the multimodal perception system, fuses the hesitation in their voice with the puzzled look on their face. It catches the mismatch between "I think I've got it" and the way they say it. Raven-1's audio-visual perception flows to the LLM layer, which decides to slow down and re-explain. Phoenix-4, the real-time facial behavior engine, renders the PAL's expression, active listening behavior, and continuous facial motion at 40fps and 1080p. The closed-loop system lets timing, perception, reasoning, and facial behavior work in concert during onboarding conversations. No single model carries the conversation alone. The intelligence layers separate a demo from a production agent. The Knowledge Base, a retrieval system that grounds PAL responses in your verified source material using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), answers off-script integration questions from your actual setup docs with roughly 30ms retrieval. Knowledge Base currently supports English-language content, which is worth factoring in for teams onboarding non-English-speaking stakeholders. Persistent Memory means a returning customer who logged off halfway through configuring single sign-on is greeted by name and picks up where they left off. Objectives and Guardrails keep the conversation moving toward a measurable goal while staying on-brand and compliant. The PAL layer works alongside your GUIDEcx or Rocketlane portal. It handles the human-facing moments around the workflow: the kickoff call, the training session and the live walkthrough. Best practices for implementing client onboarding software Tooling only pays off with a disciplined process behind it. Standardize playbooks across client segments first. One onboarding model rarely fits every customer: a strategic enterprise account, a mid-market rollout, and a tech-touch account need different levels of guidance. Build distinct tracks for high-touch, low-touch, and tech-touch segments, then automate the defaults so your implementation team starts from a repeatable baseline on every new account. Set clear ownership and milestones with real accountability. You cannot shorten the time to the first value if your team has not defined what the first value means. Define milestones with assigned owners, timelines, and SLAs by segment, anchored by a solid sales-to-CS handoff. Collect feedback at every milestone and close the loop. Poll customer-side executives and points of contact at key moments so you sense trouble early. If feedback shows customers feel overwhelmed in week one, pace the onboarding more digestibly. When you act on feedback, tell the customer, because it builds goodwill and earns you the next round of honest input. The first ninety days made human at scale An admin stuck on a setup step at 2 AM does not just need another checklist. They need to feel seen, understood, and guided through the moment where confidence can disappear. Those quiet moments are where the first ninety days become real. Onboarding has always been about helping people believe the rollout will work. See it for yourself. Book a demo.

title: Build vs. buy: how to run MCP infrastructure yourself
summary: An MCP server is easy to stand up and hard to operate. The five layers you take on when you run MCP in production yourself: hosting, analytics, testing, checks, and devtools.
body_text: TL;DR: An MCP server is easy to stand up and hard to operate. The gap is everything a web app gets for free from a mature ecosystem and MCP has no equivalent for yet. These are the five layers a team takes on when it runs MCP in production itself: Hosting : previews, TLS, custom domains, rollbacks Analytics, logs, and traces : per-tool, per-client visibility with full payloads Cross-client testing : a browser matrix where the browsers are ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor Publishing checks : store review rules with no linter Developer experience : debugging conversations you can't see Standing one up is fast. With mcp-use or the official TypeScript or Python SDK you can define a few tools and watch the inspector call them the same afternoon. Your product becomes reachable from ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and any other MCP client. Operating it is a different job, and the difference has little to do with the protocol. A web app ships with twenty years of ecosystem. An MCP server follows the model context protocol spec, which is itself evolving fast ( v2 just shipped ). Anatomy of an MCP server in production A diagram of an MCP server in production. Clients sit on top. Cross-client testing and publishing checks sit on the connection between the clients and your server. Your server sits in the middle with analytics and devtools attached on either side, and hosting is the substrate underneath. Each part is focusable and reveals a short description of the layer it maps to. Your server The part users came for The tools you set out to build. Every other box exists to keep this one reachable, observable, and shippable. Hover, tap, or focus a part to see the layer it maps to. Hosting For a web app this is solved. Push a branch and a URL exists, TLS renews itself, and rollback is a button. An MCP deploy is harder. You can't open the URL in a browser and see a page. Verifying a deploy means connecting an MCP client to it. Even if various MCP inspectors exist, people often test directly on ChatGPT/Claude themselves. The caller is an agent mid-conversation, so a slow cold start becomes a failed tool call. MCP App widgets have to resolve from a domain you own, with CSP connect - src and frame - src allowlists set correctly, before a host will render them. The result: the server passes locally and breaks when a real client connects, or the widget renders as an empty frame because the CSP allowlist misses one host. The pieces you build: Preview environments. Reviewing an MCP change means pointing a real client at a real deployment of that branch, so every branch needs a URL. Managed TLS and custom domains. Clients refuse plain HTTP, and widget domains have to be yours. Secrets split across preview and production without any of them landing in the repo. A build and deploy pipeline for your framework , kept current as the framework evolves. And it's never done: your MCP framework's next version and every transport revision can break something. How we solve: Whatever you develop with, Manufact hosting already has a preset for it: mcp-use , the official TypeScript and Python SDKs, FastMCP , tmcp , xmcp , Skybridge , or a raw Dockerfile, with an integration guide for each in our tutorials . A connected repo gets a preview URL per branch. Analytics, logs, and traces A web app logs one line per request, and wiring up Datadog or Sentry takes an afternoon. In MCP the unit of value is the tool call. A useful breakdown is per tool, per client, and per deployment revision. Payloads are full JSON-RPC bodies rather than a status code and a path, and storage grows with conversation length. That's why Manufact offers analytics designed from scratch for MCP tools, breaking down error rates and latency for each tool you expose. The pieces you build: Capture all the tool calls without adding latency. Breakdown for each client and version out there. Retention long enough to support MCP tools traces from long multi-turn conversations. Aggregates that link back to individual traces. Sample only some of the things and you lose the failing sessions. Capture everything, and you are running a log pipeline with a pretty expensive storage bill. Each new MCP surface (widgets, prompts, resources) needs its own schema before it shows up in any dashboard. How we solve: On Manufact , every exchange is captured with a shareable link, and Analytics keeps the per-tool, per-client percentiles linked to the traces behind them. Manufact then analyzes all the sessions and tries to infer the goal each user was trying to achieve , this is crucial since you don't have access to the conversation when your product is used inside ChatGPT or Claude. Cross-client testing Web apps get a solved browser matrix. Playwright runs a suite across engines and versions. For MCP, the browsers are ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor. Each sits behind a login, parses tools differently, negotiates capabilities differently, and runs its own auth flow. Testing end to end means driving authenticated sessions in the real clients (hoping you are not getting blocked as bot). Good luck running this browser infrastructure yourself only to test your MCP server. Testing against different clients is important because the behaviour of your MCP Server depends on: Different clients: works in ChatGPT, but not in Claude and Cursor. Different models: works with Claude Opus, but not with Claude Sonnet. Different devices: MCP UI tools are displayed correctly on desktop but not on mobile. Different versions: they tweak the system prompt and your MCP server stops working as expected. Here sit the bugs in your MCP server you can't spot but your users encounter. One server, four clients A panel listing six assumptions an MCP server might make about its client, with a client picker. Selecting a client shows which assumptions hold there and which fail, with a short note for each. 3/6 Picks up tool-list changes mid-conversation respects the advertised cache TTL holds Tolerates loose input schemas strict validation, rejects extras fails Waits out a slow tool call tight timeout budget fails Can ask the user for input mid-call fails the call instead fails Registers itself against your server at connect time via client metadata holds Renders your app UI renders MCP app widgets holds In ChatGPT, 3 of 6 assumptions hold. The server code is identical in all four columns. Illustrative snapshot. Real behavior shifts with every client release. The pieces you build: An authenticated session per client, kept alive. Sessions expire and captchas appear on their schedule. Eval that checks the tool call and its arguments. Assertions over a probabilistic system. The model decides whether to call your tool at all, so a test has to tolerate the run where it didn't. Validate that an MCP UI view is displayed correctly. And it's never done: clients ship UI changes and your automation breaks. How we solve: We run this as a hosted suite for the same reason: test suites that run against ChatGPT and Claude in live environments, on commits or manually. Publishing checks This is less similar to web development but closer to App Store review. The review is (still) painful but documented and with an industry of tooling around it. The ChatGPT Apps Store and Claude Cloud Connectors requirements are not so well documented, and they change FAST! Somebody on your team reads changelogs and translates them into checks by hand or in your CI/CD. The pieces you build: Protocol and discovery conformance over the transport production clients actually use. Tool schema, naming, description, and uniqueness rules matching what reviewers enforce. Read/write separation and prompt-injection hygiene in tool copy. Domain ownership, CSP allowlists, and redirect behavior for widget surfaces. Listing assets : icons, previews, structured metadata. What breaks is a rejection and the cost is the wait time, which means delaying your MCP launch or update. How we solve: That somebody in your team who keeps everything up to date is Manufact! We make sure checks stay current. Already built one? Run the publishing checklist on your MCP server Paste your MCP server URL below. We'll connect, authenticate, and run a full publishing checklist automatically. Developer experience On the web, you save a file, the page reloads, and devtools are already open. For MCP, the client is the runtime and you don't control it. There is no devtools panel inside ChatGPT. The pieces you build: Replay of a production session without asking the user for repro steps. The full request and response with timing , rather than a truncated log line. A permalink a teammate can open and see the same evidence. The reality is that you would probably end up under-testing the MCP server. How we solve: The mcp-use Inspector covers the local development. The Cloud Inspector covers the deployed MCP debugging and you can invite your QA team in the platform. When to use Manufact As MCP becomes an important part of your product surface you'll need all the infra to make sure it runs reliably. But you don't want to maintain everything yourself. The cost is attention and focus. Hundreds of teams rely on us for their MCP infrastructure and tooling and they are happy to offload all of that to focus on their product and MCP experience. When AgentMail faced this, their cofounder sized it: "Building it ourselves meant standing up hosting, auth, sessions, scaling, and monitoring. That's probably a quarter of eng time for a ten-person team, minimum. None of that makes our core product better." Adi Singh , cofounder of AgentMail Compliance sits on top. SOC 2, a pentest, data residency, zero-retention guarantees: each is its own project with its own upkeep, and none of it makes the MCP better. When to build it anyway Some teams should run every one of these layers themselves: MCP infrastructure is your product. If you sell MCP hosting, these five layers are what your team is building. A real data boundary. An on-prem requirement, a policy against external vendors, regulated data that can't leave your VPC. When the constraint is real it outweighs every efficiency argument. You have a platform team and a mature deploy pipeline, and you need one layer, not five. Building that one is reasonable. You want it on hardware you own. Most build decisions aren't made for these reasons. The demo worked on day one and you thought you could maintain it yourself. Build vs buy test Trace your own build-vs-buy call A sequential decision tree. Answer five yes-or-no questions about your team and constraints; each yes resolves to a build-or-buy verdict with a reason, and answering no to all five resolves to buy. Question 1 of 5 Is hosting MCP servers the product your team sells? The infrastructure itself is what customers pay you for. Five questions, in order. Any yes resolves the call. Where to go from here How AgentMail handles 100k+ agent tool calls with Manufact : the case study behind the quote above. How to Set Up OAuth in Your MCP Servers : the auth work every layer above assumes you've already done. Deploying Seven MCP Frameworks: A Field Report : the hosting layer, framework by framework. MCP authorization spec : what clients expect your server to implement. Still weighing build against buy? We'll walk through your stack and give you a straight answer. Book a call

title: Eton Pharmaceuticals Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Record revenue, with Q2 2026 product sales of $37.6 million, representing 99% growth over Q2 2025 Q2 2026 fully diluted GAAP EPS of $0.35, non-GAAP fully diluted EPS of $0.43; EBITDA of $14.1 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $16.2 million Raising full year revenue guidance, with 2026 revenue now
body_text: News Release Details « Back to news Eton Pharmaceuticals Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Record revenue, with Q2 2026 product sales of $37.6 million, representing 99% growth over Q2 2025 Q2 2026 fully diluted GAAP EPS of $0.35, non-GAAP fully diluted EPS of $0.43; EBITDA of $14.1 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $16.2 million Raising full year revenue guidance, with 2026 revenue now expected to exceed $145 million, up from previous guidance of more than $120 million Relaunched HEMANGEOL® May 1st, patient conversion completed ahead of schedule Acquired late-stage product candidate ASN-001, expanding the Company’s infantile hemangioma franchise, and providing a potential high-value 2027 NDA submission Submitted Prior Approval Supplement to the FDA to expand indication of KHINDIVI®, allowing for potential H1 2027 approval of expanded indication Received FDA Fast Track designation for endocrinology development product AMGLIDIA® Acquired U.S. commercialization rights to orphan drug IMPAVIDO® Management to hold conference call today at 4:30pm ET DEER PARK, Ill., Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Eton Pharmaceuticals, Inc (“Eton” or “the Company”) (Nasdaq: ETON), an innovative pharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing treatments for rare diseases, today reported financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. “Eton reported another outstanding quarter, delivering 99% year-over-year revenue growth, reflecting the strength of our rare disease portfolio and the exceptional execution of our team. Our HEMANGEOL relaunch is off to a strong start, with the patient conversion completed ahead of schedule, positioning our therapy for continued momentum and furthering our mission to allow more infants with infantile hemangiomas to benefit from timely treatment. In addition, we further expanded our commitment to the infantile hemangioma community with the licensing of ASN-001, an exciting late-stage development program that is expected to further improve care and broaden treatment options for families, while potentially becoming the largest revenue opportunity in our pipeline. The rest of our portfolio continued to deliver in the quarter, with strong contributions from our entire pediatric endocrinology franchise, including the recently launched DESMODA™, and our metabolic products,” said Sean Brynjelsen, CEO of Eton Pharmaceuticals. “Given our first half performance and strong outlook for the remainder of the year, we’re pleased to again raise our annual revenue guidance and now expect at least $145 million of revenue this year. We are also raising our adjusted EBITDA guidance, which includes the additional expenses related to the ASN-001 transaction and development. We now expect to deliver an Adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35%,” concluded Brynjelsen. Second Quarter and Recent Business Highlights Record revenues with 99% growth year-over-year. Eton reported second quarter 2026 revenues of $37.6 million, compared to $18.9 million in the prior year period, driven by the addition of sales from HEMANGEOL plus strong growth from across the portfolio. HEMANGEOL relaunched successfully, ensuring continuity of care for patients and families. The Company relaunched HEMANGEOL in May, offering full Eton Cares patient support, which provides comprehensive access and affordability services including $0 copay for all eligible patients. The transition to Eton’s program exceeded expectations, with approximately 95% of existing patients successfully transitioned by the end of June. Expanded presence in infantile hemangioma with licensing of product candidate ASN-001. Last week, Eton announced the licensing of product candidate ASN-001, which is under development for the treatment of moderate infantile hemangiomas. ASN-001 would complement Eton’s HEMANGEOL franchise and leverage the same commercial infrastructure. The Company plans to initiate a bioavailability study and anticipates a New Drug Application (“NDA”) submission upon the study’s completion in the second half of 2027. If approved, Eton believes ASN-001 offers the largest revenue opportunity in its pipeline. Strong year-over-year growth in pediatric endocrinology portfolio. DESMODA, which launched in March, continues to see strong adoption and patient growth while the three other products in the Company’s pediatric endocrinology portfolio all posted strong year-over-year revenue growth in the second quarter. The Company's adrenal franchise, consisting of ALKINDI SPRINKLE and KHINDIVI, surpassed 600 active patients on therapy, reflecting continued confidence from pediatric endocrinologists. INCRELEX continued to deliver strong growth, driven by appropriate dose optimization and sustained treatment, reflecting the Company's commitment to helping patients achieve the best possible outcomes. Completed KHINDIVI label expansion study and submitted Prior Approval Supplement (PAS) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requesting expansion of indication. The new formulation of KHINDIVI successfully demonstrated bioequivalence to ALKINDI SPRINKLE, paving the way for a potential first half of 2027 approval. The Company believes the largest unmet need for an FDA-approved oral liquid hydrocortisone remains with children under age five, and that an expanded label would dramatically increase adoption. Acquired exclusive U.S. commercialization rights to Orphan Drug IMPAVIDO. In June, Eton announced the acquisition of IMPAVIDO, a critical, life-saving medication, adding an additional 2026 product launch. The product is FDA-approved, and Eton expects to begin commercializing the product in September 2026. Pediatric endocrinology development product candidate AMGLIDIA was granted Fast Track designation by FDA. The Fast Track designation is designed to facilitate the development and expedite the review of drugs to treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need. The Company plans to initiate a bioavailability study for the product later this month and remains on track to submit an NDA by the end of 2026, allowing for potential approval and launch in 2027. Continued to advance Wilson disease franchise. In addition to a strong quarter of patient additions for GALZIN, the Company’s pilot study for product candidate ET-700, its proprietary, patent-pending, extended-release formulation of zinc acetate, is underway. The study is comparing ET-700 to GALZIN and placebo. If pilot study results are successful, Eton anticipates initiating a pivotal clinical study in early 2027. Executed INCRELEX label harmonization study agreement with Clinical Research Organization; site preparation is underway. Earlier this year, Eton received clearance from the FDA to proceed with its proposed label harmonization study, designed to support an application to broaden the approved definition of severe primary IGF-1 deficiency (SPIGFD) to match the E.U. definition. If successful, this could increase the addressable population in the U.S. from an estimated 200 to 1,000 patients. The Company has initiated study preparation activities with a goal of having the first patients dosed by the end of 2026. Guidance The Company now expects 2026 revenues to exceed $145 million, an increase from prior guidance of more than $120 million. In addition, the Company now expects to report at least a 35% Adjusted EBITDA margin, an increase from prior guidance of at least 30%. The revised Adjusted EBITDA guidance is inclusive of a $3 million licensing payment for ASN-001 which will be expensed in the third quarter, incremental second half R&D expenses related to ASN-001’s bioavailability study, and a potential, one-time $4 million commercial milestone payment related to ALKINDI SPRINKLE sales performance, which may be triggered in the fourth quarter of 2026. Second quarter Financial Results Net Revenue: Total net revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $37.6 million compared to $18.9 million in the prior year period, an increase of 99%, driven by the addition of revenue from HEMANGEOL, as well as year-over-year growth across the portfolio, in particular INCRELEX, ALKINDI SPRINKLE, GALZIN and Carglumic Acid. Second quarter 2026 revenue included $2.9 million of revenue from INCRELEX and GALZIN sales outside the United States. Gross Profit: Gross profit for the second quarter of 2026 was $25.4 million compared with $11.9 million in the prior year period, an increase of 113%, primarily due to increased product sales. Adjusted gross profit, which adjusts for the impact of acquired inventory step-up adjustments and intangible amortization, was $27.4 million in the second quarter of 2026, representing an adjusted gross margin of 73%, compared to adjusted gross profit of $14.1 million and adjusted gross margin of 75% in the prior year period. The decrease in adjusted gross margin in the second quarter of 2026 was due to higher INCRELEX sales outside the United States, which generates negative gross margin. The Company expects full year 2026 adjusted gross margin to exceed 70%, inclusive of the potential $4 million commercial milestone referred to above. Research and Development (R&D) Expenses: R&D expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $1.0 million compared to $3.7 million in the prior year period. The decrease was primarily due to the DESMODA NDA submission fee in the prior year period. The Company expects full year R&D expenses of between $10 and $14 million, with a significant increase in the second half of 2026 due to increased development activity, including the initiation of the INCRELEX label harmonization study, a $3 million expense related to the licensing of ASN-001, and incremental spending related to ASN-001’s planned bioavailability study. General and Administrative (G&A) Expenses: G&A expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $11.6 million compared to $9.7 million in the prior year period, an increase of 20%. Adjusted G&A expense, which removes share-based compensation, depreciation, transaction-related costs, and other one-time expenses, was $10.2 million in the quarter, compared with $7.6 million in the prior year period. The increase was attributable to increased headcount to support the growth of the business as well as increased cost of FDA program fees as the Company no longer qualifies for the orphan fee exemption. Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (EBITDA): EBITDA for the second quarter of 2026 was $14.1 million compared to ($0.3) million in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter of 2026 was $16.2 million or 43% of revenue, compared to $3.1 million or 16% of revenue in the prior year period. Net Income/Loss: Net income for the second quarter of 2026 was $11.6 million or $0.35 per diluted share compared to a net loss of $2.6 million or $0.10 per basic and diluted share in the prior year period. On a non-GAAP basis, the Company reported net income of $14.3 million or $0.43 per diluted share for the second quarter of 2026 compared to net income of $1.5 million, or $0.03 per diluted share in the prior year period. title: 7 AI Employee Engagement Platforms That Turn Survey Data Into Real Action
summary: Explore 7 AI employee engagement platforms that turn survey data into actionable insights, helping HR teams identify risks, improve engagement, and drive action.
body_text: Modern AI-powered employee engagement platforms have evolved beyond simple survey tools to deliver predictive analytics, real-time interventions, and actionable insights that directly impact retention and organizational performance. • Real-time listening beats periodic surveys : Platforms using continuous conversational AI capture sentiment at critical employee milestones, achieving up to 90% response rates compared to traditional annual surveys, with the ability to predict attrition 60-90 days before resignation occurs. • Silent employees represent hidden flight risk : Workers who don't actively engage with feedback channels are 3x more likely to quit than vocal employees, making AI-powered detection of behavioral shifts and sentiment patterns critical for proactive retention strategies. • Action speed determines engagement impact : Organizations deploying targeted interventions within 30 days of survey completion see 2.3x higher engagement improvement than those who delay, yet only 34% of companies actually take action on survey results. • Integration drives adoption and ROI : Platforms embedded in existing workflows (Slack, Teams, HRIS systems) achieve significantly higher usage rates and deliver measurable returns, with some organizations reporting 224% ROI and saving 75% of HR team time on analysis. • Platform selection depends on organizational maturity : Growth-stage companies benefit from modular solutions like Lattice (starting at ₹1,096.95/seat), while enterprises with dedicated analytics teams gain value from comprehensive platforms like Qualtrics that unify 24+ data sources for predictive modeling. The shift from reactive dashboards to proactive intervention represents the fundamental difference between platforms that collect data and those that drive measurable business outcomes. Organizations must evaluate whether their current approach captures feedback when it matters most—at the moments that determine whether employees stay or leave. inFeedo AI's Amber: AI-Powered Employee Engagement Platform for Real-Time Action Image Source: inFeedo AI What Makes inFeedo AI Stand Out inFeedo AI's Amber operates as an AI-powered Chief Engagement Officer that moves beyond traditional annual surveys to capture employee sentiment across every milestone. 330+ CHROs globally trust the platform. Amber reaches employees from onboarding through exit and uses conversational AI to create a space where feedback happens continuously rather than once a year. The platform draws from 9 years of People Science research and 80M employee responses. It applies a framework with 7 drivers and 45 elements that workplace psychologists validated. This foundation separates Amber from generic survey tools that rely on templated questions without scientific backing. The system has 26 psychologist-designed templates that adapt to specific organizational contexts and measure experience with reliability across different employee populations. The platform's proprietary PTM (People-To-Meet) algorithm makes it effective. This predictive model analyzes sentiment patterns, behavioral shifts and silence to identify employees at risk of leaving. Silent employees present a specific challenge. They're 3x more likely to quit than those who engage. Amber flags these individuals early, groups them by risk levels and routes managers to intervene before attrition occurs. Key AI Features for Survey Action Planning Amber's continuous listening system captures feedback at milestone-specific moments rather than waiting for scheduled survey windows. The platform monitors language shifts over time and connects individual sentiment to manager relationships and team dynamics. Amber initiates conversations tailored to those exact moments when employees complete their first month, change projects or experience leadership transitions. The AI doesn't stop at data collection. Amber auto-summarizes employee conversations, creates manager-specific action plans and generates board-ready reports. These summaries provide context-rich insights that help leaders understand not just what employees feel but why sentiment shifted and what actions will address concerns. The system sends AI-powered acknowledgment emails to close the feedback loop and shows employees their input produced tangible outcomes. Report Studio delivers decision-ready analytics with AI summaries, multiple data filters and automated scheduling straight to leadership inboxes. Teams can slice data across 50+ filters to identify patterns within specific cohorts, departments or locations. This workflow integration transforms how HR teams move from insight to intervention quickly. Organizations that previously lost 60 out of 100 at-risk employees within six months due to inaction now have a solution. Real Results: How Companies Reduced Turnover Genpact deployed Amber across 130,000 employees with measurable impact on retention. Employees who engage with Amber are 2x more likely to stay at the organization. The platform became the only non-financial metric driving bonus pools for 200+ leaders at Genpact. This demonstrates executive confidence in AI-driven engagement data. Organizations using Amber improved their engagement scores by as much as 24.8% in just one quarter. The platform achieves a 90% response rate on surveys, substantially higher than traditional engagement tools. Employees experience an 11-point increase in overall engagement when grievances are heard and resolved. The system's predictive capabilities surface early warning signs 60 to 90 days before resignation. Amber tracks trajectory rather than isolated snapshots by connecting what employees said months ago to current feedback. This longitudinal view catches the decline that point-in-time surveys miss and gives managers time to address issues before departure becomes inevitable. Best For: SaaS Companies and Enterprise Teams inFeedo Amber scales for organizations deploying across distributed teams, hybrid setups and field operations. The platform supports multilingual conversations across 34 languages and maintains compliance with GDPR, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. Companies in 60+ countries use Amber with SSO and API connectors for enterprise-grade security. SaaS companies benefit from Amber's integration capabilities with Slack, Microsoft Teams, HRIS platforms and ATS systems. The platform fits into existing workflows rather than creating another data island. Amber captures insights across remote and in-office employees without requiring separate survey instruments for IT and software organizations managing hybrid setups. Enterprise teams gain value from knowing how to identify localized problems that combined scores mask. A company-wide engagement score of 80% can hide a single team operating at 35% under a manager driving departures. Amber surfaces these patterns early and connects sentiment shifts to specific reporting structures and team dynamics that need intervention. Culture Amp: AI-Driven Pulse Surveys and People Analytics Image Source: Culture Amp Platform Overview and Core Capabilities Culture Amp positions itself as the employee experience platform serving 6,000+ organizations globally. The platform draws from 1.6 billion questions answered and creates the largest source of engagement and performance data worldwide. This dataset feeds back into the platform and provides leaders with standards and insights confirmed in a variety of industries and geographies. The system operates on what Culture Amp calls CultureOS™, an intelligence layer that connects culture and performance data. The layer is grounded in people science and increased by AI. The Performance Culture Quadrant™ sits at the core, a framework that maps the path to peak performance by connecting engagement confidence with performance confidence. Organizations use this quadrant to identify whether teams fall into engaged skepticism, peak performance, disconnected, or strained categories. Culture Amp maintains 40+ survey templates covering engagement, retention insights, DEI, onboarding, offboarding, and pulse surveys. Each template stems from organizational psychology research rather than generic question sets. The platform achieved a 90% original employee engagement survey participation rate and saves teams 20+ hours per month on survey distribution and reporting. Platforms like inFeedo excel at continuous conversational AI that captures sentiment at every milestone. Culture Amp focuses on periodic measurement combined with performance management. The difference matters to organizations deciding between immediate intervention and structured feedback cycles. AI Features for Employee Engagement AI Coach accelerates high performance through instant insights in both Engage and Perform modules. The system delivers three specific capabilities: Engagement Analysis : AI Coach surfaces focus areas from engagement survey data and quickly identifies themes, trends, and hidden opportunities rather than presenting raw dashboards. The tool analyzes survey responses to provide clear next steps, not just data visualization. Managers receive tailored guidance on where to focus action based on their team's specific feedback patterns. Comment Summaries : The platform provides instant, unbiased summaries of employee comments and automates analysis that previously required manual review. Teams can analyze survey results in seconds and generate shareable reports to leadership. This AI-powered analysis helps HR teams focus resources on meaningful work rather than data processing. Performance Review Support : AI Coach helps managers create personalized, balanced, and practical performance reviews faster. The system uses expert coaching and guided role play to prepare managers for complex conversations. This reduces the time managers spend crafting reviews while improving quality and fairness. The AI functionality increased manager and HR team productivity, though Culture Amp doesn't specify the exact percentage. Organizations report that AI Coach makes managers' lives easier by providing built-in coaching for situations they haven't encountered before. Only 57% of employees believe their company will act on survey results, a figure declining yearly since 2021. The gap between feedback collection and action remains wide. Platforms focused on continuous feedback loops, like inFeedo's approach, address this differently than periodic survey tools by closing the loop immediately rather than waiting for quarterly cycles. Integration and Automation Options Culture Amp integrates with every major HR SaaS product in the market. The platform connects with HRIS systems, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and flow-of-work tools to sync employee data automatically. This eliminates manual data entry and frees HR teams to focus on strategy rather than administration. The platform offers 40% faster implementation for Enterprise Performance Management compared to competitors. Support has 24/5 product support, a dedicated support center with resources, and developer documentation. Organizations access these resources whatever tier they choose and ensure consistent service quality. Security compliance covers SOC II, ISO 27001, and GDPR standards. Culture Amp protects confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all systems and data entrusted by customers and employees. Annual billing structures apply to all products, with pricing dependent on employee count, product selection, and service tier. Ideal Use Cases Culture Amp serves organizations with 200-999 employees through to enterprise deployments of 1000+ employees. The platform works in professional services, financial services, software and technology, and manufacturing sectors. Organizations prioritizing structured performance management alongside engagement measurement find value in the full platform integration. The system suits teams needing deep benchmarking against industry standards, access to organizational psychology expertise, and tools that blend engagement data with performance reviews, 1-on-1 conversations, and goal management. Companies already using Microsoft 365 might compare Culture Amp's standalone platform against Microsoft Viva's native integration. Organizations requiring predictive turnover modeling should review whether Culture Amp's periodic surveys provide sufficient early warning compared to continuous listening platforms that flag risk 60-90 days before resignation. It intervenes at every employee milestone and turns survey data into immediate action rather than quarterly reports. The 90% response rate and 2x retention improvement speak to results that matter. How do AI employee engagement platforms predict which employees are likely to leave? AI platforms analyze patterns in employee feedback, sentiment shifts, behavioral changes, and engagement levels to identify early warning signs of attrition. Advanced systems use predictive algorithms that can flag at-risk employees 60-90 days before they resign, giving managers time to intervene. These platforms track factors like declining engagement scores, reduced participation in surveys, changes in communication patterns, and specific feedback themes that historically correlate with turnover. Q2. What makes continuous listening more effective than annual employee surveys? Continuous listening captures employee sentiment at specific moments throughout their journey—onboarding, project changes, manager transitions—rather than waiting for scheduled annual surveys. This approach achieves significantly higher response rates (often 90% versus typical 30-40% for annual surveys) because employees provide feedback when experiences are fresh and relevant. It also enables real-time intervention to address issues before they escalate into resignation decisions, whereas annual surveys often identify problems months after they've already caused damage. Q3. How do these platforms ensure employee anonymity while still providing actionable insights to managers? Modern engagement platforms use aggregation techniques and confidentiality thresholds to protect individual identities while surfacing team-level trends. They provide managers with insights about their team's overall sentiment and specific themes without revealing who said what. Some platforms enable anonymous two-way conversations where employees can share sensitive feedback about management or compensation while maintaining complete privacy. The systems only display data when there are enough responses to prevent identification of individuals. Q4. What ROI can organizations expect from implementing AI-powered employee engagement tools? Organizations typically see measurable returns including 2x improvement in employee retention rates, 15-24 point increases in engagement scores within quarters, and significant time savings (50-75% reduction in analysis time for managers and HR teams). Some platforms report 224% ROI based on reduced turnover costs alone. Companies also experience productivity gains, with highly engaged employees being 3x more productive and 84% less likely to seek other jobs, directly impacting business outcomes and customer satisfaction. Q5. Which type of organization benefits most from AI employee engagement platforms? Organizations with distributed or hybrid workforces, high turnover costs, and commitment to acting on employee feedback gain the most value. SaaS companies, enterprises with 200+ employees, and organizations in competitive talent markets see particularly strong results. Companies already using modern HR tech stacks and those willing to integrate engagement data with performance management, learning systems, and daily workflows maximize their investment. The platform choice depends on whether you need real-time intervention, predictive analytics, or integration with existing systems like Microsoft 365 or Workday.

title: Flex LNG – Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Release
summary: Flex LNG is an LNG shipping company with a fleet of thirteen modern LNG carriers on the water, all with the latest generation two-stroke propulsion (MEGI and X-DF). Flex LNG is listed on New York Stock Exchange and Oslo Stock Exchange under the ticker FLNG.
body_text: August 19, 2026 Hamilton, Bermuda Flex LNG Ltd. (“Flex LNG” or the “Company”) today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Highlights: * Vessel operating revenues of $106.8 million for the second quarter 2026, compared to $80.5 million for the first quarter 2026. * Net income of $44.9 million and basic earnings per share of $0.83 for the second quarter 2026, compared to net income of $19.5 million and basic earnings per share of $0.36 for the first quarter 2026. * Average Time Charter Equivalent (“TCE”) rate of $86,119 per day for the second quarter 2026, compared to $65,729 per day for the first quarter 2026. * Adjusted EBITDA of $79.0 million for the second quarter 2026, compared to $53.2 million for the first quarter 2026. * Adjusted net income of $42.5 million for the second quarter 2026, compared to $16.9 million for the first quarter 2026. * Adjusted basic earnings per share of $0.79 for the second quarter 2026, compared to $0.31 for the first quarter 2026. * The Company declared a dividend for the second quarter 2026 of $0.75 per share. The dividend is payable on or about September 17, 2026 to shareholders, on record as of September 3, 2026. Marius Foss, CEO of Flex LNG Management AS, commented: “In the second quarter of 2026, we generated revenues of $106.8 million, or $102.7 million excluding EU Allowances, our highest quarterly revenue since the fourth quarter of 2021. Fleet-wide Time Charter Equivalent earnings were $86,119 per day, compared with $65,729 per day in the first quarter. Adjusted net income was $42.5 million, resulting in adjusted earnings per share of $0.79, an increase of 155% from the first quarter. Energy markets have experienced significant volatility in recent months, as hostilities in the Middle East disrupted the broader energy complex. The resulting volatility and trading inefficiencies created attractive opportunities for our two spot-exposed vessels, Flex Volunteer and Flex Artemis. We secured employment for both vessels covering the second and third quarters, and each contributed to the increase in revenues. Both vessels are currently being marketed for spot and term employment from the end of the third quarter of 2026, leaving us with approximately 89% firm contract coverage for the remainder of the year. In addition, Flex Aurora commenced her two-year firm charter with a supermajor in late March 2026. The charter runs until 2028 and includes three successive two-year extension options. We therefore benefited from a full quarter of earnings from the vessel during the second quarter. Likewise, Flex Constellation completed her first full quarter under her new 15-year charter. These two vessels made a solid contribution to both revenues and earnings. Looking ahead to the remainder of 2026, we expect the freight market to remain volatile. On the supply side, around 55 vessels were delivered during the first seven months of the year, and shipbrokers expect a further 40 to 45 vessels to enter the fleet before year-end, hence, fleet growth is expected to remain high. At the same time, several demand-side factors could provide support to the market. European gas storage levels are currently at multi-year lows of around 61% as of mid August, while the shortfall in Qatari export volumes is contributing to the redirection of U.S. export volumes toward Asian importers. Despite the reduction in Qatari volumes, global LNG exports are flat year-on-year, supported by solid growth in U.S. export volumes and strong growth from West African exporters. Against this backdrop, we are entering an interesting and potentially volatile period for the LNG shipping market, with the balance between continued fleet growth and competition on LNG volumes between Europe and Asia. However, we maintain our full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $345 – $370 million, excluding EUAs. We also maintain expected fleet-wide TCE earnings of $73,000 – $78,000 per day. Our guidance range for adjusted EBITDA is $255 – $280 million. Supported by a strong earnings outlook for 2026, substantial contract backlog and a robust balance sheet, including $397 million of cash and no debt maturities before 2029, the Board is pleased to declare another quarterly dividend of $0.75 per share, equivalent to an aggregate distribution of approximately $41 million, marking our twentieth consecutive ordinary quarterly dividend of $0.75 per share. Including special dividends, we will have returned approximately $850 million to shareholders since 2021.” Second Quarter 2026 Results Presentation In connection with the earnings release, a video webcast will be held today at 15:00 CEST (09:00 a.m. EST). title: Custom Web Development Services in 2026: What Matters, Costs, and Smarter Alternatives
summary: See what custom web development services cover in 2026, the real costs, and why workflow-driven CRMs are now the smart pick for flexible, cost-effective growth.
body_text: TL;DR: Custom web development services in 2026 combine tailored workflows, technology choice, and integration capability, but you pay for flexibility. For organizations with high process complexity or CRM spend, workflow-driven custom CRMs, like Miniloop, now offer both cost savings and infrastructure control over agency or platform builds. Custom Web Development Services in 2026: What Matters, Costs, and Smarter Alternatives Last updated: August 2026 Generic website templates are losing appeal for organizations that demand control over workflows, data, and long-term cost structure. Rising SaaS costs, regulatory pressure on data ownership, and the rapid evolution of e-commerce and CRM requirements mean that custom web development is no longer just a branding luxury. It's an operational need. In 2026, buyers face a clear tradeoff: settle for packaged e-commerce suites, or own a solution built around what the business actually does. But most agencies still focus on building websites, not solutions that reduce operational costs or integrate deeply with your business logic. Are custom web development services worth the investment in 2026? Custom web development is no longer a luxury reserved for large enterprises. title: Pennsylvania American Water Completes Acquisition of the Sutersville-Sewickley Municipal Sewage Authority Wastewater System
summary: Acquisition delivers lower average rates and long-term infrastructure upgrades MECHANICSBURG, Pa., Aug. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pennsylvania American Water today completed its acquisition of the...
body_text: Acquisition delivers lower average rates and long-term infrastructure upgrades MECHANICSBURG, Pa. , Aug. 13, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Pennsylvania American Water today completed its acquisition of the Sutersville-Sewickley Municipal Sewage Authority (SSMSA) wastewater system for $3.25 million. The newly acquired wastewater system serves approximately 500 customer connections in Sutersville Borough and Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. "Pennsylvania American Water is pleased to welcome Westmoreland County residents as new wastewater customers," said Pennsylvania American Water President Justin Ladner. "We look forward to providing these communities with safe, reliable wastewater service by delivering on our technical expertise and extensive wastewater experience." As part of the agreement, Pennsylvania American Water plans to invest approximately $700,000 in improvements to the SSMSA system to improve the quality and reliability of service over the next five years of ownership. The company has a long and successful track record of providing solutions for water and wastewater systems facing significant capital investment needs and making the necessary and continued investments to meet current and future regulatory requirements. Learn more at pennsylvaniaamwater.com/infrastructure . "Three and a half years ago, the Sutersville-Sewickley Municipal Sewage Authority welcomed a new board as the members who had overseen the system for more than 20 years stepped down. After evaluating all available options, the board determined that Pennsylvania American Water was best positioned to operate, maintain and invest in the system for the benefit of our customers," said SSMSA Chairman Bruce Riley. "Both the Borough of Sutersville and Sewickley Township have supported the decision to sell the system to Pennsylvania American Water." SSMSA's decision in May 2025 to sell its wastewater system to Pennsylvania American Water was made with customers in mind. The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PUC) approved the acquisition on March 26, 2026. Prior to the acquisition, SSMSA aligned its rates with the Pennsylvania American Water rates in effect at that time, which results in a lower monthly bill for customers with average household usage. As the PUC regulates the company's rates and service rules, any future changes to rates must be reviewed and approved by the PUC. Pennsylvania American Water offers several customer assistance programs, including its longstanding H2O Help to Others Program™ , which provides income-eligible customers with grants of up to $500 per year, significant discounts on monthly bills, arrearage forgiveness and water-saving devices and education. About American Water American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn , Facebook , X and Instagram . About Pennsylvania American Water Pennsylvania American Water, a subsidiary of American Water, is the largest regulated water utility in the state with approximately 1,200 dedicated employees working to provide safe, clean, reliable and affordable water and wastewater services to approximately 2.5 million people. (the “Company” or “Dorman”) (NASDAQ: DORM), a leading supplier in the motor vehicle aftermarket industry, today announced its financial results for the second quarter ended June 27, 2026. Kevin Olsen, Dorman’s Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer, stated, “Our second quarter results included record earnings and strong cash flow generation, reflecting both solid operating performance and the recovery of IEEPA tariff costs recognized in prior periods. Year-over-year, net sales for the quarter increased 1% to $545 million, diluted EPS increased 53% to $2.93, and adjusted diluted EPS increased 50% to $3.08. We believe our cash flow generation positions the company well to make strategic investments and drive long-term growth. “Given our performance through the first half of the year and targeted pricing actions we are taking as a result of a more stable tariff environment, we are updating our full-year 2026 guidance. title: Best AI Tools to Replace Characters in Videos (2026): Tested and Ranked
summary: Honest comparison of the best AI character replace tools in 2026. Magic Hour, Akool, Viggle AI, and others tested for quality, free access, and commercial use. Ranked by use case.
body_text: Quick Answer AI character replacement lets you swap the person in an existing video with another person or character while keeping the original movement, timing, and scene. For the easiest free browser-based option, Magic Hour is the best free option for quick, browser-based character replacement , with no sign-up required and free generations up to 3 seconds ; for professional marketing teams, Akool is better suited to higher-volume commercial workflows. TL;DR Magic Hour: Best free option for browser-based character replacement with no sign-up. The free plan supports clips up to 3 seconds and adds a watermark to free results, with support for real people, cartoons, and anime references. Akool: Best for professional marketing and A/B testing with different spokesperson looks. Viggle AI: Best for motion-driven character animation and full-body swaps, rather than the traditional replacement workflow. Cuty AI: Best for single-person replacement with natural blending into the original scene. Vidnoz: Best for replacing multiple faces in one video. Remaker AI: Best for long video files and batch face-replacement workflows. Introduction You may want to swap a person in existing footage without reshooting the scene, opening complicated VFX software, or hiring a production team. But “AI character replacement” covers several different workflows: some tools replace the whole character in existing footage, some animate a still image using motion from another video, and some only replace faces. We will compare six tools based on their free-tier access, supported workflows, output quality, and published usage limitations. Character Replace vs Character Animation vs Face Swap: Know the Difference First Before choosing a tool, it helps to define what you actually want to change. Tool Type What It Does Best For Character Replace Replaces the full person in existing video with a reference image while keeping the original motion Swapping actors, ad localization, mascot content Character Animation Takes a still image and makes it perform movements from a reference video Animating a character that does not exist in video form yet Face Swap Only Changes the face in a video while keeping the original hair and body Quick face swaps without full character transformation This article focuses mainly on the first category: replacing the character already in your footage. If you only need to change a face, see Magic Hour's Face Swap Video tool ; if you want to animate a still character, the Viggle section below explains how that workflow differs. Comparison Table Tool Free Without Sign-Up Full Character Replace Works in Browser Watermark on Free Results Cartoon/Anime Reference Commercial Use on Free Plan Best For Magic Hour Yes Yes Yes Yes* Yes No Free browser-based character replacement Akool No Yes Yes Yes Limited / model-dependent No Professional marketing Viggle AI No Yes, full-body Yes Free tier varies Yes Yes Motion-driven character swaps Cuty AI No Yes Yes Yes Yes No Clean single-person replacement Vidnoz No Primarily face replacement Yes Free tier varies Limited No Multi-face replacement Remaker AI No Face-focused Yes Yes Limited Check tool-specific terms Long videos and batch face swaps Magic Hour's current free plan is intended for testing and applies a watermark; paid plans remove the watermark and unlock commercial use. Key takeaway: Magic Hour is the most straightforward option here if your priority is starting in a browser and replacing a full character with either a realistic or stylized reference. The 6 Best AI Character Replace Tools 1. Magic Hour Best for: Free browser-based character replacement with no sign-up Magic Hour Character Replace is built specifically around replacing the subject in existing footage while preserving the source performance. You upload a video and a reference image, and the model generates a new version with the replacement character; it supports real people as well as cartoons, anime, and illustrated characters. The tool also offers Character mode for changing the subject while keeping the scene intact and Scene mode for regenerating the subject and background together. A useful shortcut is the built-in preset gallery, which includes characters such as Peter Griffin, Kratos, Elmo, Deadpool, Chun-Li, and the Grinch, making it easy to test the workflow without preparing a reference image. The main limitation is that difficult footage—especially heavy motion blur, occlusion, or fast cuts—can still introduce flicker or character drift. Free plan: Yes Watermark on free results: Yes Full character replace: Yes Starting paid price: $15/month Magic Hour's Creator plan is currently $15/month when billed monthly and includes watermark-free exports and commercial use. 2. Akool Best for: Professional marketing teams running A/B tests with different spokesperson looks Akool positions Character Swap as a professional workflow for marketing, advertising, entertainment, and production teams. Its Character Swap system has two modes: Replace , which transfers a character into a video, and Animate , which uses a still character image and applies motion from a reference video. Its API documentation supports clips up to 120 seconds and output up to 1080p for the Character Swap workflow. The platform is a strong fit for teams creating multiple versions of campaigns or testing different talent and character looks. The tradeoff is that Akool's licensing and pricing are more business-oriented, while its free tier is intended for personal use and includes restrictions compared with paid plans. Free plan: Yes Watermark on free results: Yes Full character replace: Yes / model-dependent Starting paid price: $12/month 3. Viggle AI Best for: Animating a character image with motion from a reference video Viggle AI is worth including, but it needs an important distinction: its core strength is body swap and motion-driven character animation , rather than the classic “replace the actor in my existing footage while keeping the shot” workflow. You can provide a character image and a video, and Viggle maps the character's appearance onto the video's movement. Its current body-swap page says it supports full face-and-body replacement, anime, 2D, 3D, and cartoon characters, as well as multi-person swaps. That makes it excellent for memes, dance clips, character performances, and motion references. However, if your goal is specifically to replace an actor in an existing production shot while preserving that shot's original visual identity, a dedicated character-replace workflow is usually the better match. Free plan: Yes Watermark on free results: Varies by workflow Full character replace: Yes, full-body Starting paid price: $9.99/month 4. Cuty AI Best for: Clean single-person replacement with natural blending Cuty AI offers a dedicated Video Character Replace workflow that automatically identifies the subject and replaces it with a reference character while preserving the background, motion, and action. Its main appeal is simplicity: upload the source video, provide the reference, and let the model handle subject identification and blending. Cuty AI has a free plan, but free outputs include a watermark and commercial use is reserved for paid plans. Free plan: Yes Watermark on free results: Yes Full character replace: Yes Starting paid price: $6.9/month 5. Vidnoz Best for: Multi-face replacement in a single video Vidnoz has several related workflows, including AI Character Swap and dedicated video face-swap tools. Its current Face Swap tool supports both single-face and multiple-face video replacement, making it particularly useful when a clip contains several people. The important limitation is that Vidnoz's dedicated face-swap workflow is not the same as full character replacement: the primary operation changes the face while retaining the original body and appearance. Its broader AI Character Swap offering is more focused on avatar-style character changes and talking-video use cases. Free plan: Yes / limited Watermark on free results: Yes / varies by tool Full character replace: Face-focused Starting paid price: $9.99/month 6. Remaker AI Best for: Long video files and high-volume replacement workflows Remaker AI is particularly useful if file size and video length are your main constraints. Its Video Face Swap tool accepts files up to 500MB and 30 minutes , while its batch workflow can process multiple videos. Remaker is primarily a face-swap platform rather than a full actor-replacement system, so it should not be treated as identical to Magic Hour Character Replace. It does, however, offer multi-face video swapping and a credit-based system, with new users receiving free credits and additional credits available through daily check-ins. Free plan: Yes / limited Watermark on free results: No on many current face-swap tools Full character replace: Face only Starting paid price: $5.99/month Which Tool Should You Use? Choose Magic Hour if you want browser-based character replacement that works with real people, cartoons, and anime references without starting with an account. Choose Akool if you're a marketing team creating professional campaign variations and need a broader production platform. Choose Viggle AI if you have a character image and want that character to perform specific motion from a video reference. Choose Cuty AI if your priority is a straightforward single-person replacement workflow with the original scene preserved. Choose Remaker AI if you are working with unusually long video files or need batch face-swapping rather than full character replacement. A Note on Consent and Responsible Use Only replace a person in a video with someone else's likeness if you have their consent or have the right to use the reference image. Avoid creating replacement content that falsely presents a real person as saying or doing something they did not actually say or do. Always check each platform's current terms before using generated content publicly or commercially. Frequently Asked Questions What is the best free AI tool to replace a character in a video? For a true character-replacement workflow, Magic Hour is one of the easiest places to start because it runs in the browser and supports both realistic and stylized reference characters. Its free plan is intended for testing and includes watermarked outputs; commercial use and watermark-free exports require a paid plan. Is Viggle AI a character replace tool? Viggle can perform full-body character swaps, but its workflow is different from a conventional actor-replacement tool. It is especially strong when you have a character image and want to transfer the motion of another video onto that character. Can I replace a character in a video with a cartoon or anime character? Yes. Magic Hour explicitly supports cartoon, anime, and illustrated reference images, while Viggle also supports realistic, anime, 2D, 3D, and cartoon character styles. Cuty AI's Character Replace workflow can also use a reference character image. Do any of these tools work without downloading software? Yes. Magic Hour, Akool, Cuty AI, Vidnoz, and Remaker AI all work in a web browser. Viggle AI uses a Discord-based workflow, so it is the exception. Can I use the output commercially? Yes, but commercial rights depend on the tool and plan. Magic Hour, Akool, Cuty AI, Vidnoz, and Remaker AI do not include commercial use on their free plans, while Viggle AI allows commercial use of its generated content, including on its free tier.
